A1.justification: Both complete 10-page PDFs describe the same CoMet research, with readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting reliable comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original CoMet experiments on MVTec-AD, VIADUCT and KSDD2, including benchmark results, component ablations and training-contamination tests in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5.

after.justification: v2 retains the original experimental results, ablations and robustness tests reported in Tables 1–5 and Figure 5.

M1.justification: The confidence weights, covariance-dependent regularization, meta-learning updates and DifferNet/SimpleNet integrations in Sections 3 and 4.4–4.5 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use MVTec-AD, VIADUCT and KSDD2 for image-level and pixel-level anomaly detection. Nominal-only training and contaminated-training scenarios are retained without changes in coverage.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain their respective comparator sets. Figure 5 still compares the CoMet variants with IRP, MLD-IR, DifferNet and SimpleNet.

E3.justification: The reported metrics and settings remain unchanged, including 256×256 inputs, 180 training epochs, batch size 192 and learning rate 0.0002. The robustness evaluation retains training-contamination levels from 0% to 10%.

E4.justification: Table 5 retains the same component-removal ablations, and Figure 5 retains the same contamination-robustness analysis. No supplementary analyses or case studies are added or removed.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests for the experimental results. Statistical uncertainty reporting is unchanged.

E6.justification: All result entries in Tables 1–5 and the plotted results in Figure 5 are unchanged. For example, CoMet-SN retains 99.7% I-AUROC on MVTec-AD and 90.3% on VIADUCT, while CoMet-NF retains 94.9% on KSDD2.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, assumptions and equations (1)–(16) are unchanged. No theorem, proof or derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about model-agnostic training on uncurated data, robustness to anomalous training samples and state-of-the-art performance.

C2.justification: The explanations involving boundary-sample downweighting, regularization, the recall–precision tradeoff and dataset-specific performance are unchanged. No substantive limitation or applicability qualification is added.

D1.justification: v2 adds a GitHub code-access link to the abstract, absent from v1. Implementation details and hyperparameters otherwise remain unchanged; the PDFs alone do not establish the repository's contents or usability.

R1.justification: Both versions contain the same 30 references and unchanged related-work discussion and research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds the short code-availability statement and updates the arXiv version/date header. The remaining wording, terminology and section sequence are unchanged.

P2.justification: The added abstract text causes limited reflow on pages 1–4, including moving the Section 3 heading from page 3 to page 4. All five figures and five tables retain their content and display structure.

improvement.justification: The new code link provides an explicit implementation location absent from v1, modestly improving reproducibility documentation and discoverability. Scientific content and evidence remain unchanged. Repository completeness and successful reproducibility cannot be assessed from the supplied PDFs.
